title: [graph] map with downstream_join_id double-fires the join on a non-empty iterable
author: slavashvets

comments.author: pydanty[bot]
comments.body:
<!-- pydanty:status-comment:v1 -->

**Classification:** bug

**Why this matters:** Users who use `downstream_join_id` as documented get a silently wrong result on non-empty graphs: the run returns the reducer initial value instead of the reduced mapped result.

**Evidence summary:** The issue includes a runnable minimal reproduction showing that `add_mapping_edge(..., downstream_join_id=collect.id)` makes the join fire twice (`[[], [1, 2, 3]]`) and returns `[]`, while a plain `.map()` returns `[1, 2, 3]` once. The reporter verified on latest beta and stable. Repository research found no duplicate or prior fix.

**Next action:** PR-ready. A localized guard in the mapping-edge join dispatch is the likely fix; the PR opener will reproduce and add a regression test.

comments.author: clavedeluna
comments.body: I think I know the solution to this. There's a duplicate reducer created because it's keyed by the map fork's run id instead of the join parent fork run id.
